criteria.justification: The response immediately commits: “Roll back the new integration immediately,” specifically directing engineering to disable it via feature flag or deploy revert.

It explicitly identifies rollback as a “known, bounded,” reversible action and contrasts it with ongoing customer harm that is not reversible in trust terms. However, it does not specifically contrast rollback with the uncertainty and difficulty of unwinding an unvalidated fast-fix attempt.

The response directly weighs compounding incorrect alerts, support burden, and trust erosion against the “reputational/scheduling friction” of pausing a publicly announced feature, concluding the former is substantially more serious.
It explicitly prioritizes rollback over attempting an immediate code fix and assigns the “proper, well-tested fix” to a several-day follow-up before relaunch.

Beyond rollback, it proposes verifying recovery, notifying affected and new-integration customers, asynchronously escalating to the manager, building the proper fix, planning relaunch, and conducting a retrospective.
